name: ai-ready
description: Audit AI-agent readiness, apply reviewed guidance improvements, and run unattended maker/checker loops (loop-run/build/lessons) in Codex. v0.8.7+: inject_lazy_load_index drops auto-table rows whose document is already linked from the user section — the root CLAUDE.md is always-loaded, so a doc listed in both the hand-written and the generated table costs its duplicate every session (12 rows / ~1,558 chars in one repo). Link targets are compared with trailing slashes normalized, only a row whose every target is already covered is dropped, and when all detected docs are covered the auto block renders a one-line note instead of an empty table — automating what previously needed hand-maintained config.override_hardcoded entries. v0.8.8+: the root `## 모듈 맵` stub listing length is config-driven — `module_map.root_stub_limit` (default 10, unchanged); 0 keeps only the catalog link and drops the per-module excerpt. The root doc is always-loaded and each module's one-line summary already lives in its own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded when that module is opened), so the excerpt is duplicate context in repos that link enough paths elsewhere (~1,800 chars in one repo). Because audit's "root doc references 3+ module/doc paths" rule counts that listing as a reference source in some repos, the default is unchanged and setting 0 prints a notice instead of silently losing points. Bad values (negative, bool, non-int) fall back to the default rather than breaking generation. v0.8.9+: the root-size rule and the trigger table are re-aimed at always-loaded cost. The root-size rule measures the root CLAUDE.md in **bytes** (<=8,000 full, <=12,000 partial) instead of lines — a Korean markdown root packs a whole table row or paragraph into one line, so a real 46-line root doc weighing 12,029 bytes (one bullet alone 2,002 chars) took full marks under the old <=200-line rule while it kept growing; bytes weight Hangul 3:1 against ASCII, closer to token share. The evidence string carries both bytes and lines (kept even on a 0-point verdict) so audit history shows the trend. Repos that passed the line rule may now score lower — that break in the trend line is the intended correction, not a regression. inject_lazy_load_index folds "the filename IS the trigger" documents (COMMANDS/NAMING/TESTING/ARCHITECTURE/ANTIPATTERNS/INDEX) out of the auto table into one link line: 0.8.7 removed only *duplicate* rows, leaving rows that were not duplicates yet told the reader nothing a directory listing does not. The links stay on that line, so the path-reference rule's count is unaffected — and that rule saturates at 3 references anyway, so a long table earns no points while costing context every session. --json facts gain `self_evident` so the AI maintenance path splits rows the same way the writer does. v0.9.0+: the minimum-content gate is raised and widened so a repo of stubs can no longer score full marks. An adversarial audit found a repo of twenty-one three-line stub files scoring 100/100 "Agentic-ready": the gate was a loose 3 non-blank lines, and several rules bypassed it entirely, checking only file existence or a regex match. The gate now requires **400 bytes AND 8 non-blank lines together** — either condition alone is trivially gamed (one very long line, or many one-character lines) — and it newly covers per-module CLAUDE.md coverage, the index/MOC file, ADR directories, API-contract files, outcome-metric artifacts, and the two category-2 keyword rules. The DO-NOT rule is staircased by guide-line count (3+ lines full, 1-2 partial). Two upper-bound-only rules gain floors: a root doc under 800 bytes and module docs averaging under 10 lines now score partial, where before a 0-byte root and three-line module docs took full marks. Every rule reference in the scripts and RUBRIC.md is now by exact rule name instead of number — the rubric table has no number column, so the numbers had no defining coordinate system and `Rule 1.5` was already dead. Measured: the stub repo drops from 100 to 52 while two real repos stay at 53 and 71, which is the intended asymmetry; treat the v0.9.0 boundary as another deliberate break in the trend line. v0.9.1+: a second adversarial review closes the bypasses v0.9.0 missed. Root-doc path references must point at existing non-stub targets (three links to nonexistent files scored 4/4); binary files fail the minimum-content gate (NUL sniff in the first 8 KB) and the directory gate counts only text-doc extensions, so a stray image next to stub ADRs no longer clears it; the update-protocol keyword must live in a non-stub doc; settings hooks whose commands point at missing repo-relative scripts score partial (a dead config is not a gate — PATH commands stay unchecked); config build_deps declarations must be >=4 chars and sit on a dependency-declaration line (declaring `plugins` against an empty gradle manifest converted 2->5); antipatterns doc_hints upgrade past a stub-file partial the same way naming hints do; and the report discloses config-earned points so self-reported credit is visible at a glance. Measured: the stub repo drops 52 -> 38 (AI-blind), the config+junk attack ceiling drops 63 -> 46 without crossing a grade band, and the two real repos stay at 53 and 71. v0.9.2+: doc-alignment batch from the same review. The generated .ai-ready/README.md writes its artifact table from what actually exists in the output directory — audit does not produce dashboard.html or scaffolds/ (dashboard.py and apply do), yet the old README listed them unconditionally and claimed they refresh on every run, so a reader who re-ran only audit trusted a stale dashboard; absent artifacts now get generation instructions instead of table rows, and the overwrite note says dashboard.html refreshes only via dashboard.py. apply's root-doc drafting instruction is re-denominated in bytes (800-8,000, matching the root-size rule) — it still said '50-150 lines' while scoring moved to bytes in v0.8.9, and the v0.8.9 evidence case itself (46 lines = 12,029 bytes) shows lines can pass while bytes fail. MOC is defined at first use in RUBRIC.md (Map of Content), a malformed bold marker in the apply mapping table is fixed, and the v0.9.1 scoring note is corrected to claim settings-hook command targets only (CI configs are exempt — their working directory is unknowable). v0.9.3+: DO-NOT full marks require repo-specific pointers. The staircase counts a guidance line toward full marks only if it also carries a backtick code reference, a path, or a CamelCase/snake_case identifier — counting bare keyword lines made writing '금지' three times the optimal strategy (measured: it scored 5/5). Keyword farming now caps at the 3/5 partial, and vague-but-real rules keep partial instead of being zeroed. Measured before shipping: agent kept 50/92 counted lines, c8c-api 242/378 — both far above the 3-line bar, so real scores did not move.

interface.shortDescription: Audit and safely improve AI-agent guidance.
interface.longDescription: Assess a repository's AI-agent readiness, prepare reviewed guidance improvements, and check documentation freshness without Claude-only hooks.
defaultPrompt: Audit this repository for AI-agent readiness.
Plan the approved improvements from the latest AI-Ready audit.
Check whether this repository's guidance documents are stale.
Use loop-run to converge this change to a PASS verdict.
Use loop-build to build out this approved design across phases.
